text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid has said the country was still in a financial predicament, though the caretakers had pulled it out of a state of near-bankruptcy.
- Nawaz Sharif has been unanimously elected leader of the parliamentarty parties of the Pakistan Muslim League (PML), Awami National Party, Jamiat Ulema-e-Pakistan and independents.
- Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda has offered the hand of friendship to Pakistan and said both countries suffered because of their bitter rivalry over disputed Kashmir.

- The PML and the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) have agreed in principle to offer the post of Sindh province governor to MQM Senator Aftab Sheikh and provincial assembly's speakership to the MQM MPA-elect Kazi Khalid, it was learnt.

- The Pakistan People's Party parliamentary group has decided to contest elections for the slot of the leader of the house, speaker and deputy speaker, setting at rest rumours that it might stay away from the proceedings.
- Football makers in Sialkot have pledged to stop using child labour, under an agreement signed between International Labour Organisation and the Sialkot Chamber of Commerce.

- Nawaz Sharif, whose PML scored a big victory in February 3 elections, has asked all national and provincial assembly members of his party to declare their assets and give an undertaking that "they would not do any business" as long as their party is in power.

- The government has turned down the request of the Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) to delay transaction or increase the conversion premium of the five-year bonds (exchangeable into shares) of the Pakistan Telecommunications Company Ltd.
- Fruit exports during the first seven months of the current fiscal year registered a growth of 108.30 percent compared with the corresponding period of the previous year.
- The average dividend pay-out of 18 cement plants listed on the KSE showed a dismal picture with returns falling to six percent in 1996 from 38 percent in 1994
- While the other financial indicators are showing signs of recovery, foreign direct investment has still been stagnant depicting no fresh commitments over the past two months.
- Three shiploads of sugar have been booked for import by the private sector at the rate of $345 per tonne from Thailand and India.
